one_liner: Intel 8080 and PDP-11 assembly decompressors for the LZSA1/LZSA2 formats; code no longer publicly reachable, no speed figures.
what_it_does: DeLZSA was Ivan Gorodetsky's set of hand-written assembly routines that unpack LZSA1 and LZSA2 streams (produced by the emmanuel-marty/lzsa compressor) on Intel 8080 and PDP-11 machines. It is a port of the decoder to two retro CPUs that the LZSA repo itself does not cover (its asm/ folder has 6502, 65816, 6809, 8088, x86 and Z80 only), not a replacement for the C reference decompressor. The repo, its owner account, its raw README and its 2019 GitLab predecessor (gitlab.com/ivagor/lzsa8080, with a PDP11 subfolder) all return 404 as of 2026-10-07, so the API shape (entry registers, in-place support, block or raw format) cannot be documented.
how_it_is_fast: Not documented: no source or README could be read. Any speed comes from the LZSA format itself, which is byte-aligned and avoids 16-bit arithmetic on 8-bit CPUs; the LZSA README puts LZSA1 at about 90% and LZSA2 at about 75% of LZ4 decompression speed on 8-bit systems (ZX7 at 47.73%), measured on its own Z80/6502 decoders, not on DeLZSA.
when_to_use: You are writing software for an Intel 8080 or KR580-class machine, or a PDP-11 family machine, want LZSA-packed assets, and can obtain a copy of Gorodetsky's routines from another source.
You want a reference for porting the LZSA2 nibble-and-token decoder to a CPU without an existing LZSA routine and the code turns up again.
Retro or demoscene projects where packed size matters more than decode speed (LZSA2 compresses about as well as ZX7 on the LZSA README corpus).
when_not_to_use: Any modern-CPU workload: this is retro-CPU assembly; use the LZSA C decompressor, LZ4 or zstd instead.
Anything that needs code you can vendor today: the GitHub repo, the owner account and the GitLab predecessor are all gone, so there is nothing to copy and no license.
Z80, 6502, 65816, 6809, 8088 or x86 targets: the LZSA repo ships its own size- and speed-optimized decoders for those.
When you need a measured speed or size figure for the 8080 or PDP-11 routine: none was ever seen.

integration.dependencies: none known (assembly routines; code not reachable)
integration.min_toolchain: not documented (an 8080 or PDP-11 assembler; dialect unknown)
integration.platforms: Intel 8080 and PDP-11 per the LZSA README link text; nothing else documented

gotchas: Dead link: github.com/ivagorRetrocomp/DeLZSA, github.com/ivagorRetrocomp and raw.githubusercontent.com README paths (HEAD, main, master) all return 404; the 2019 GitLab home gitlab.com/ivagor/lzsa8080 returns '404 Project Not Found' and GitLab has no user named ivagor.
The listed baseline is not comparable: the LZSA reference decompressor is portable C for modern machines, while DeLZSA targets 8080 and PDP-11, so 'faster than baseline' has no defined meaning here.

The only nearby numbers are LZSA format figures from the LZSA README (LZSA1 90%, LZSA2 75% of LZ4 decode speed on a ZX Spectrum and C64 file set), measured with other people's Z80/6502 decoders; that README's text also says LZSA1 decompresses 'faster than LZ4 on 8-bit systems' while its own table shows 90% of LZ4_HC -19 -B4 -BD.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Only when the target is an 8080 or PDP-11 and you can find the routines elsewhere; for every other CPU use the decoders shipped in LZSA itself, and on modern machines LZ4 or lz4ultra give faster decoding with maintained code.
verified_claims_summary: No benchmark exists: nothing was measured for DeLZSA against the LZSA reference decompressor or anything else, and the code cannot be inspected. The record is kept at tier D as a pointer from the LZSA README's External links.
status_note: Gone: repo, owner account and GitLab predecessor are all 404 (last seen linked from the LZSA README, whose last change was 2023-02-13), license unknown, so it is reference-only with nothing to vendor.
